fit.population: FBS vs FBS completed, DEV only (2016 has no frozen sigma)
fit.selection:
Rule fixed before the comparison was read: a key-number method must
    (a) improve the push log loss at integer closing lines (point estimate
    < 0) and (b) not worsen the cover log loss with a CI entirely above zero.
    Among methods that pass, the one that moves the pure cover probability the
    LEAST (mean |p_method - p_t| at the closing line) is used, because the
    cover probability is the calibrated quantity the decision engine prices and
    a key-number adjustment has no business moving it away from key numbers.
    If neither passes: the plain t with the tie mass sent to overtime margins.

method_text: pure Student t (mean = pure margin, frozen sigma, df) discretised at k +/- 0.5; tie mass to the overtime margin distribution; bin k gains (r_|k| - 1) P(k), taken half from each neighbouring integer (|k| = 1 from |k| = 2); clipped at 0, renormalised
